extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (educational institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, compliance officers, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and final regulatory provisions defining who qualifies as a 'confidential employee' under Title IX and the recipient and employee obligations for notification, duties, scope, and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: First category of 'confidential employee' — privileged or confidential communications
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee whose communications are 'privileged or confidential' under Federal or State law; confidential status is 'for purposes of this part' and applies only to information received while the employee is functioning within the scope of their duties to which privilege or confidentiality applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised from only 'privileged' to 'privileged or confidential' to encompass statutory/constitutional confidentiality that may not rise to formal legal privilege. Confidential employees under this category need not report conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination to the Title IX Coordinator, and a recipient does not have Title IX knowledge if the only person who knows is a confidential employee. However, other laws (e.g., mandatory reporting laws) may require disclosure to persons other than the Title IX Coordinator; such disclosures are permissible under Title IX if not in conflict with Title IX or this part. The Department removed references to an employee's 'role' as unnecessary given the focus on duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second category of 'confidential employee' — designated to provide services related to sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee whom the recipient has designated as confidential for the purpose of providing services related to sex discrimination; the employee's confidential status applies only to information received in connection with providing those services and is clarified as being 'under this part.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include (but is not limited to) guidance counselors, organizational ombuds, or on-campus sexual assault response center staff. Recipient may designate any number of such confidential employees (no regulatory cap). Department replaced 'designated as a confidential resource' with 'designated as confidential' to reduce confusion and made non-substantive phrasing edits. The confidential designation does not preclude that the employee may have unrelated duties that are non-confidential; confidentiality is limited to service-related disclosures. Recipients are not required to designate confidential employees (see §106.44(d)(1) discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third category of 'confidential employee' — employees conducting IRB-approved postsecondary research
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee of a postsecondary institution conducting an Institutional Review Board (IRB)-approved human-subjects research study designed to gather information about sex discrimination; confidential status is 'only with respect to' information received while conducting that study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes researchers employed by one recipient conducting studies approved by another institution's IRB. Does not extend to non-employees or employees of research institutions unaffiliated with the recipient; Title IX obligations are limited to the recipient. The Department declined to expand to climate-survey personnel or to remove this category. Recipients are not required to notify participants of third-category confidential employees due to the dynamic nature and limited scope of such research teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient notification requirement (§106.44(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient has any confidential employees, the recipient must notify all participants in its education program or activity of how to contact its confidential employees (rather than requiring notice of identities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient has discretion to decide what contact information to provide (e.g., name, title, office, phone number). The Department declined to prescribe a notification method because methods may be inapplicable or burdensome in particular contexts. The requirement excludes notifying participants of third-category (IRB researcher) confidential employees. Recipients are not required to designate at least one confidential employee, and nothing prevents recipients from providing off-campus support information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements of confidential employees (§106.44(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee must explain their status as confidential 'for purposes this part' and must explain the circumstances in which they are not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.44(d)(2) requires confidential employees to: (i) explain their confidential status and circumstances when it does not apply (including when they may have mandatory reporting obligations); (ii) provide information about how to contact the Title IX Coordinator and how to make a complaint of sex discrimination; and (iii) explain that the Title IX Coordinator may offer/coordinate supportive measures and may initiate informal resolution or investigation procedures. These requirements apply to all three confidential-employee categories. The Department declined to require researchers to include this information in informed consent but notes they may choose to do so. Recipients may supervise and train confidential employees and may use self-attestation mechanisms that do not disclose confidential details to verify compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality does not negate other legal reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Being designated 'confidential' for purposes of Title IX does not exempt an employee from complying with Federal, State, or local laws that mandate reporting (e.g., child abuse mandatory reporting laws).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures of personally identifiable information obtained in complying with this part are generally prohibited but exceptions exist when required by Federal law, when permitted by FERPA, or when required by State/local law if not in conflict with Title IX. The Department clarifies that a confidential employee may nonetheless be required by other law to disclose information and that such disclosures are permissible under Title IX unless they conflict with Title IX or this part. See discussion of §106.44(j) for permissible circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training expectations for confidential employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to add specific additional training topics for confidential employees beyond the training requirements in §106.8(d); the topics in §106.8(d)(1) are considered sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to mandate trauma-informed training specifically, reasoning that the regulations already incorporate principles preventing reliance on stereotypes and that flexibility allows recipients to tailor training to their community. §106.8(d)(1) requires employees to be trained on the recipient's obligation to address sex discrimination, scope of sex discrimination (including 'sex-based harassment'), and applicable notification/information requirements under §§106.40(b)(2) and 106.44. Recipients retain discretion in how to meet these training requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation: confidentiality tied to duties rather than 'role'
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential status applies only to information received while the employee is functioning within the scope of their duties to which privilege or confidentiality applies; references to an employee's 'role' were removed as unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that confidentiality is not a blanket status tied to a job title but is limited to the context of the employee's duties that carry privilege/confidentiality. This helps avoid directing disclosures to employees whose confidential protection may not apply to particular types of disclosures (e.g., athletic trainers whose privilege applies only to treating patients).

rubrics_metrics.name: No limit on number of designated confidential employees and no requirement to designate
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not impose a limit on how many employees a recipient may designate as confidential, and the Department declines to require recipients to designate at least one confidential employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognized resource constraints (especially for smaller schools, elementary, and secondary schools) and determined that requiring designation could be unduly burdensome or infeasible. Recipients must, however, treat any employees who fall within the first or third categories as confidential for Title IX purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and labeling of confidential employees (scope of notice and characterization)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to identify only confidential employees 'best positioned' to help, to require naming confidential employees by category, or to label confidential employees as complainant- or respondent-supporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department concluded that listing all employees who fall within the first and second categories is less burdensome and less confusing than attempting to subjectively identify 'best' employees. It also expressed concern that limiting identification could disincentivize employees from fulfilling Title IX responsibilities. Nothing prohibits recipients from providing additional, more tailored information if they choose.
